rationale: The student confuses the face number with minutes because they have not internalized counting by 5s for each clock number. Using rhythmic skip-counting by 5s connects each step to multiples of 5 so they see that 4 jumps of 5 equals 20 minutes, not 4.
intent: Generate skip-counting by 5s from 0 up to 60 with visual jumps. Frame the jumps as counting minutes around a clock face, focusing on steps like 1 jump (5), 2 jumps (10), and 3 jumps (15), ensuring the student practices the sequence without directly repeating the exact target problem of 4 jumps = 20.

data.title: Clock Time Leaps by 5s
data.description: Count along by 5s up to 60 to see how minutes increase at each step around a clock face.

character.imagePrompt: A friendly orange kangaroo wearing a tiny pocket watch.

challenges.instruction: Watch our kangaroo hop by 5s from the very start at 0!
challenges.hint: Count every time the kangaroo lands: 5, 10, 15...

challenges.instruction: Continue watching the hops as we count the first few minutes on the clock.
challenges.hint: Keep following the rhythmic jumps up to 20.

challenges.instruction: Watch the hops grow as we reach halfway around the clock face to 30.
challenges.hint: Every hop adds 5 more minutes to our time.

challenges.instruction: Keep counting past thirty minutes. Notice how the ones digit alternates between 5 and 0.
Almost all the way around the clock! Watch the hops up to 55.
challenges.hint: Counting by 5s makes telling time super fast.

challenges.instruction: Complete the full circle around the clock face all the way to 60 minutes!

judgement.reasoning: The student confuses the face number with minutes (thinking 4 means 4 minutes rather than 4 groups of 5 minutes). While skip-counting by 5 on a number line is a helpful prerequisite, this activity is purely a linear skip-counting watch/count-along runner that does not explicitly map clock numbers (1, 2, 3, 4...) to the minutes (5, 10, 15, 20...). Furthermore, the tasks are passive 'count_along' animations. However, it does provide a different visual representation (number line) of multiples of 5 up to 60 with clock context in text.
judgement.verdict: This detour reviews counting by fives on a number line, but without explicitly mapping the clock hand's numbers (1 to 12) to those minutes, it misses the crucial bridge needed to fix the student's misconception.
